key_insight: General-purpose LLMs outperformed domain-specific pretrained models for alloy property prediction, with further gains from numerical estimates supplied by prior models.
engineering_relevance: Combining general-purpose LLMs with existing predictors and carefully selected reference data could reduce the cost of alloy property screening.
method: Benchmark general-purpose LLMs against SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, and SciBERT across Ti, steels, high-entropy alloys, and Al.
Prompt DeepSeek V3.1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash with CatBoost or SteelBERT estimates to guide prediction correction.
Evaluate reference-data similarity and self-reported confidence alongside prediction accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that using only 5% of high-similarity training references achieved performance similar to using the full training set, while high self-reported confidence correlated with smaller errors.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical error metrics or detailed out-of-distribution results, so robustness on unfamiliar alloy compositions remains to be verified.
paper_title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction
